atoms.text: Most children in ancient Egypt did not go to school. Instead, they learnt the family trade at home. Only children from rich families needed to go to school, as they had to learn to read and write in order to work government jobs.

While boys were learning the family trade, girls would learn how to do household tasks like mending clothes. Sometimes, they had to learn the family trade as well, meaning they were doing double the work!

atoms.a: Why did rich children need to go to school?
atoms.hint: More than one answer can be correct.

atoms.a: What might ancient Egyptian girls be taught?
atoms.hint: More than one answer can be correct.

feedback.end: They would also often do water sports on the Nile, such as rowing or even “water jousting”!

instruction.text: What type of game do you think this is?

atoms.b: The ancient Egyptian board game of Senet was played on a board with ((++30 3)) squares. The goal was to get all the ((++pieces peaces)) of your colour off of the board.
Instead of rolling dice, players would throw four painted sticks. Each stick was white on one side and ((++black purple)) on the other.
atoms.sound: Instead of rolling dice, players would throw four-painted sticks. Each stick was white on one side and black on the other.

atoms.b: For every ((++stick die)) that landed with the white side facing up, you could move a piece one square.

text: This shows how the board would start, and the direction that pieces moved in.

instruction.text: Imagine you are at the end of a game of Senet. There are only two pieces left, and it’s your opponent’s turn! Their piece is currently on the purple square. Select the square that it will move to.

text: Remember, for every white stick you have, you move one square. The blue arrow shows the direction pieces move in.

feedback.finish: Your opponent has landed on a special square called the House of Water! When this happens, the piece must go all the way back to the square marked with an ankh.

instruction.text: Now it’s your turn! Your piece is currently on the blue square. Select the square that it will move to.

text: Remember, for every white stick you have, you move one square. The blue arrow shows the direction pieces move in.

feedback.finish: You have landed on a special square called the House of Happiness! Every piece must first land here before continuing.

instruction.text: A few turns later, and you’re nearly at the finish line!

text: Remember, for every white stick you have, you move one square. The blue arrow shows the direction pieces move in.

atoms.a: To win, you need to get your final piece off the board. How many white sticks will you need to do this?

atoms.text: Lucky you! You have thrown 3 white sticks!

feedback.finish: You have beaten your opponent and won the game of Senet! Why don’t you try making a board of your own?
